question: Honeywell reported Q2 2026 a few weeks after spinning off Aerospace. What were consolidated sales vs sales excluding Aerospace, and why is GAAP EPS from continuing operations so far above adjusted EPS?
grading: Use HON, CIK 773840. Consolidated sales USD 9,719M; ex-Aerospace sales USD 5,187M. Identify the Quantinuum gain removal (-$15.87/share) as the main EPS adjustment. State actual Q2 close June 27, spin June 29 in Q3, and Aerospace consolidated in Q2 with discontinued-operations presentation beginning Q3. Keep consolidated and ex-Aerospace EPS bases distinct.
answer: HON consolidated Q2 2026 sales were USD 9,719 million; sales excluding Aerospace were USD 5,187 million. Consolidated GAAP continuing-operations EPS of $17.83 reconciles to adjusted EPS of $4.52, principally by removing $15.87 per share of Quantinuum deconsolidation gains; other net adjustments add $2.56. Ex-Aerospace EPS was $16.65 GAAP / $1.95 adjusted. The Q2 actual close was June 27, although presented as June 30: the June 29 Aerospace spin occurred in Q3. Aerospace remains consolidated in this Q2 presentation and becomes discontinued operations beginning Q3. [G25-E1, G25-E2]

**Question:** Honeywell reported Q2 2026 a few weeks after spinning off Aerospace. What were consolidated sales vs sales excluding Aerospace, and why is GAAP EPS from continuing operations so far above adjusted EPS?
*As of 2026-10-01*

| | Sales (USD millions, GAAP as reported) | GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations (USD) | Adjusted EPS (USD, non-GAAP) | Sales (USD millions, non-GAAP basis) | GAAP EPS from continuing operations (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consolidated (including Aerospace Technologies) — Q2 FY2026, quarter ended June 30, 2026 | $9,719 [1][2] | $17.83 [1][2] | $4.52 [1] | — | — |
| Honeywell Technologies (excluding Aerospace Technologies) — Q2 FY2026, quarter ended June 30, 2026 | — | — | $1.95 [1] | $5,187 [1] | $16.65 [1] |

- Honeywell Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) consolidated sales of $9,719 million on a GAAP as-reported basis, and those consolidated results include the operations of Honeywell Aerospace, which separated in a spin-off on June 29, 2026. [1][2]
- Sales excluding Aerospace Technologies (the Honeywell Technologies non-GAAP basis, which adjusts reported net sales from continuing operations for separation impacts and removes sales attributable to the Aerospace Technologies business) were $5,187 million in Q2 FY2026, up 3% reported and up 4% organic. [1]
- Consolidated GAAP diluted earnings per share from continuing operations were $17.83 in Q2 FY2026, versus adjusted EPS of $4.52, a gap of 13.31 per share. [1][2]
- On the Honeywell Technologies basis (excluding Aerospace), GAAP EPS from continuing operations were $16.65 in Q2 FY2026 versus adjusted EPS of $1.95, a gap of 14.70 per share. [1]
- The gap between GAAP and adjusted EPS is driven by the one-time gain on deconsolidation of Quantinuum, which added $15.78 after tax per share in Q2 FY2026, partially offset by higher divestiture-related costs of $1.54 after tax per share. [3]
- The Q2 FY2026 per-share amounts have been retrospectively adjusted for the one-for-two reverse stock split that took effect June 29, 2026, and adjusted EPS for the quarter used weighted average shares of 318.6 million. [1][3]
- The Aerospace business's results are expected to be reflected as discontinued operations beginning in Q3 FY2026, so the Q2 FY2026 consolidated figures that still include Aerospace are not directly comparable to the recast presentation. [1][3]

**Not available**
- Q3 FY2026 (quarter ending September 30, 2026) consolidated or ex-Aerospace sales and EPS: Q3 FY2026 has not been reported as of 2026-10-01; the evidence contains no Q3 FY2026 actuals. [1]
- A dollar amount of the Quantinuum deconsolidation gain (only a per-share after-tax amount is disclosed): The evidence quantifies the gain only as $15.78 after tax per share; no total dollar gain is printed in the provided evidence. [3]
